Genomic Analysis Protocols

Step-by-step protocols for population-level genomic analysis, built from shared operations and swappable methods.

  • Are these cases related to each other?
  • When did this outbreak start, or when was the pathogen introduced?
  • Was this introduced once, or several times?
  • Is drug resistance spreading between cases?
All 5 questions →

How the site is organized

3 Protocols An ordered set of operations for a specific goal, such as surveillance of a pathogen group. Steps can restrict which methods are allowed. uses 6 Operations A general analytical step defined by what it does, like genome alignment or phylogenetic inference. done by 15 Methods A specific, swappable way to carry out an operation, with its implementations. Each method links back to the protocols that use it.

Protocols

  • Bacterial phylogenomic surveillance

    Determine how bacterial isolates are related to one another from whole-genome SNP phylogenies, for cluster detection and outbreak investigation.

    1. Read preprocessing
    2. Site masking (optional)
    3. Genome assembly and variant calling
    4. Recombination filtering (optional)
    5. Phylogenetic inference
  • Fungal phylogenomic surveillance

    Determine how fungal isolates are related to one another from whole-genome SNP phylogenies, for cluster detection and outbreak investigation.

    1. Read preprocessing
    2. Site masking (optional)
    3. Genome assembly and variant calling
    4. Phylogenetic inference
  • Viral phylogenomic surveillance

    Determine how viral genomes are related to one another from whole-genome phylogenies, for lineage tracking, introductions, and transmission, including segmented viruses.

    1. Read preprocessing
    2. Genome assembly and variant calling
    3. Genome alignment
    4. Phylogenetic inference
